newsitem.title: UK: Bone marrow transplant saves unborn baby.
newsitem.headline: Bone marrow transplant saves unborn baby.

text.p: Italian doctors said on Friday they had saved an unborn baby by doing a bone marrow transplant while it was still in the womb.
The baby had a rare genetic defect that would have left him without a functioning immune system.

The mother's first son had died of the same defect, X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency, and the only chance of saving the second child would have meant keeping him in a germ-free tent until a bone-marrow transplant could be done.
Dr Fulvio Porta and colleagues at the University of Brescia offered the mother another option -- an experimental bone-marrow transplant in the womb.
It worked, they reported in the Lancet medical journal. The baby was given a transplant of his father's bone marrow and was still healthy three months after birth.
He had plenty of white blood cells, central to the immune system, produced by his father's bone marrow.
"Our report should encourage applications of this method to other inherited disorders curable by bone marrow transplant," Porta's group wrote.

Other operations are now frequently done on unborn babies, including heart surgery. Because the immune system of a foetus is not fully developed, such undertakings often work better because there is less chance of rejection. There is also less chance of scarring.
